analysis.evidence: In וְכָל הַחַיָּה לְמִינָהּ, כָל quantifies the collective singular הַחַיָּה. The phrase לְמִינָהּ ‘according to its kind’ supports the distributive reading ‘and every wild animal according to its kind.’
analysis.morphology: וְ־ ‘and’ prefixed to a masculine singular construct noun.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists כָל הַחַיָּה לְמִינָהּ, “every wild animal according to its kind,” alongside הַבְּהֵמָה, “the livestock.” Each group has its own לְמִינָהּ, marking wild animals and livestock as distinct groups.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun with the definite article הַ־, used collectively.
analysis.sense: wild beast, beast of the field

analysis.evidence: In וְכָל הַחַיָּה לְמִינָהּ, the suffix ־ָהּ refers to the feminine singular הַחַיָּה. The phrase groups the wild animals by kind.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ + masculine singular construct noun מִין + third-person feminine singular suffix ־ָהּ.

analysis.evidence: In וְכָל הַבְּהֵמָה לְמִינָהּ, כָל governs the definite collective noun הַבְּהֵמָה, yielding “and all the livestock according to their kinds.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed conjunction וְ.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists הַחַיָּה (wild animals) and הַבְּהֵמָה as separate groups, each followed by לְמִינָהּ (according to its kind). In this list, הַבְּהֵמָה denotes livestock collectively.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In וְכָל הַבְּהֵמָה לְמִינָהּ, the suffix ־ָהּ refers to the feminine singular collective הַבְּהֵמָה ‘livestock’. The same phrase follows הַחַיָּה just before it, grouping each class of animals by kind.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ expressing classification + masculine singular construct noun מִין + third-person feminine singular possessive suffix ־ָהּ.

analysis.evidence: וְכָל quantifies הָרֶמֶשׂ ‘creeping thing’. The phrase includes every creature that creeps on the ground, and לְמִינֵהוּ ‘according to its kind’ groups those creatures by kind.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed conjunction וְ ‘and’.

analysis.evidence: In וְכָל הָרֶמֶשׂ, כָל quantifies the marked noun. The following participle הָרֹמֵשׂ describes what these creatures do, and עַל הָאָרֶץ specifies where they move. The phrase names a class of animals in the verse’s list.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ plus a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: הָרֹמֵשׂ agrees in gender, number, and definiteness with the collective noun הָרֶמֶשׂ. The phrase עַל הָאָרֶץ specifies where the creatures move, yielding “that moves about on the ground.”
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, with the prefixed definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: In הָרֹמֵשׂ עַל הָאָרֶץ, “that creeps on the ground,” עַל introduces הָאָרֶץ as the surface on which the creature moves.
הָרֶמֶשׂ הָרֹמֵשׂ עַל הָאָרֶץ describes creatures that crawl on the ground. The preposition עַל identifies the ground as the surface on which they move.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of common gender, singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: The suffix refers to הָרֶמֶשׂ in כָל־הָרֶמֶשׂ הָרֹמֵשׂ עַל־הָאָרֶץ, “every creature that creeps on the ground.” The phrase classifies these creatures by kind, following the same pattern as לְמִינָהּ with הַחַיָּה and הַבְּהֵמָה earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ + masculine singular construct noun מִין + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־ֵהוּ.

analysis.evidence: In וְכָל הָעוֹף לְמִינֵהוּ, הָעוֹף is a definite collective meaning “the birds.” The marked word includes the whole group, “and all the birds,” which לְמִינֵהוּ then groups by kind.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular construct noun.

analysis.evidence: In וְכָל הָעוֹף לְמִינֵהוּ, “and all the birds according to their kinds,” הָעוֹף names a class alongside the other animal classes. The following כֹּל צִפּוֹר, “every bird,” clarifies the collective sense.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute collective noun.

analysis.evidence: In וְכָל הָעוֹף לְמִינֵהוּ, the suffix refers to the masculine singular collective הָעוֹף. The phrase groups the birds by kind, repeating the pattern used for the preceding animals.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ prefixed to a masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: כֹּל governs the singular צִפּוֹר in כֹּל צִפּוֹר, “every bird.” The phrase expands וְכָל הָעוֹף לְמִינֵהוּ, “and all the flying creatures according to their kinds.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 7:14, כֹּל צִפּוֹר כָּל כָּנָף follows וְכָל הָעוֹף לְמִינֵהוּ (“and every flying creature according to its kind”). The repeated כֹּל and the reference to wings include birds of every kind, regardless of size.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of common gender, singular construct, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כֹּל צִפּוֹר כָּל כָּנָף, the marked כָּל governs the singular כָּנָף ‘wing’. The phrase describes birds of every kind of wing, continuing the verse’s enumeration by kind.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל כָּנָף means “every wing.” It follows כֹּל צִפּוֹר (“every bird”) and refers to winged creatures by their wings.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.
